why: No avenue, agreed. But a Brandt-matrix ENTRY is a class-level (not genus-level) representation number of a quaternary form, so 'genus layer / true at squares' is not the right reason. The correct kill is B2 Thm 2.2(i): quaternion-order encodings in B_{p,∞} are two-coordinate slices, i.e. the tied-divisor event; positivity of the entry is that event.
A three-term Croot count producing 4/p for each p is literally ES; Croot's engine needs many terms (Bloom Prop 1) and at k=3 its local step is the ET parametrisation. Circular is correct.

Eisenstein>(1-ε)·cusp with a power-size main term on a p^{o(1)}-to-one encoding contradicts B3 (CONDITIONAL_ES Prop 2.3, rel. ET Thm 1.1) for almost all p. Known-false for the stated quantitative form.

Polylog Type II witness modulus and polylog both-endpoint forest windows are false i.o. unconditionally (POINTWISE_OMEGA13 Thm 5.1; H4_NOT_POLYLOG). Row correctly points to the surviving one-coordinate window HC(p) (FRONTIER §7.2).

Checked the Type I size lemma: (4a−1)yz = pa(y+z), p∤yz ⇒ p | 4a−1 ⇒ a ≥ (3p+1)/4 for p≡1(4); correct. But the claim 'optimal solution has p | max' is not equivalent to ES (it is vacuous where no solution exists); it is a STRENGTHENING of Type-II existence (implies a Type II solution wherever a Type I one exists). Label should be harder-than-open (ES-II strength), yield none. Not a false negative.
should_be: harder-than-open (implies Type II existence at essentially every p); calibration only; plausibility 0

why: Finitely many polynomial certificate families cannot cover the square classes (Mordell–Schinzel, unconditional); degree/height comparisons are inside B1 Prop A.

A fixed rounding rule with finitely many variants is linear in p on each class mod k: a finite union of polynomial identities, excluded on square classes by Mordell–Schinzel unconditionally (B1 Prop A).
Any rule reading only p mod M is a finite congruence covering; square classes are not coverable (Mordell–Schinzel).
RG reading of HJ length is vocabulary for ES₅ ⟺ λ(p) ≤ 3 with certificate sign; no new statement.

Lenstra's divisors-in-residue-classes bounds/finds hits, never proves existence; the remaining statement is a (★) hit in the range C > √p/4, a sub-event of the tied-divisor event (strictly stronger than (★)).
Verified the identity ((4x−p)y−px)((4x−p)z−px) = p²x² from (4x−p)yz = px(y+z); each conic fibre is one divisor-in-class event = B2 slice.

Agreed no avenue, but 'known-false' is overstated: the privacy lemma (SS8 2.3) only excludes pooling large primes across shifts; it is not a theorem that no p→q persistence rule exists (the row's note concedes this). The Pass-1 statistic (72.1% vs 73.8%) is EVIDENCE of absence.

Cited reasons do not apply. An affine closure 'ES(n) ⇒ ES(an+b) on a class' used with strong induction (ES(p) from ES((p−b)/a), all smaller n assumed) is a recursive procedure of depth ≍ log p, not a finite formal run, so B1 Thm M/Mordell–Schinzel do not cover it; T1 does not bind either because ES(m²) is true by scaling. Not refuted. Real constraints: the map must transform an ARBITRARY solution of n (no algebraic relation between U_n and U_{an+b} over ℤ is known), and must be 4-specific (8/131 fails). Open but no handle.
should_be: unclear/open (implausible): plausibility 1, novelty 1; constraints = numerator-8 test + no known integral correspondence U_n ⇢ U_{an+b}

why: Fixed small-B menu fails i.o. CONDITIONAL on Dickson ((J)83, (J)106). Label should carry 'CONDITIONAL' but the verdict is right; the row's coverage curve is useful EVIDENCE.
12/p for all p>12241 implies ES(p); it is ES plus extra (strictly stronger, same lottery at lower mean, 4|12 so full T1). 'Circular' acceptable (better: harder-than-ES).
Value-preserving 2-for-2 rewrites from a 3-term solution give reachability only ((J)82); from signed/relaxed starts they are |d|-preserving reflections (barred, (J)89 Cor 4.2) or a new B2 event.
Union over (a,d) of genus/class conditions is Type I itself; finite sub-unions are congruence coverings (Mordell–Schinzel). Genus condition on f is automatic.

No avenue, agreed; but 'CM point maps to a positive integral point of U_p' is not known false — it lacks any candidate map. The precise kill is B2 Thm 2.2(i) (Heegner/Hecke encodings are slices) plus B3 for the equidistribution step.

why: Products of primes ≡ 1 (mod 4) are ≡ 1 (mod 4), never ≡ −1 (mod 4C): sum-of-two-squares factors can never be the certificate divisor. Correct elementary obstruction.

Chowla over ℤ is open and in any case averages over n (B6); no implication Chowla ⇒ R(p) ≥ 1 exists, and large-q FF ES fails generically so FF Chowla is no model. Plausibility 0 justified; 'yield none even granting Chowla' is the more precise label.
W(p) ≤ C·ℓ(p)^κ + GRH (ℓ(p) ≤ 2log²p) gives polylog W(p), contradicting POINTWISE_OMEGA13 Thm 5.1. Known-false CONDITIONAL on GRH (label should say so).
A prime N ≡ 1 (mod 4C) has only divisors 1, N ≡ 1, never ≡ −1 (mod 4C): prime values are certain failures. Elementary and correct.
Exact zero of a fractional part over the trial set is R(p) ≥ 1 (trial form); discrepancy bounds work at scales ≫ the 1/m exact-hit probability (B3).
One-interval Chowla/sign patterns are open even for λ; and λ-data decides parity, not divisor class (CLASS_FORCING Thm 2.1).

Bounded-degree multisections over square classes are excluded (Mordell–Schinzel/T1); an unspecified growing-degree multisection is just 'a solution exists' (restatement). Note: structured growing-level identity families are B2 hatch H-A, which is NOT ruled out — but the item supplies no structure.
should_be: circular (as stated); H-A remains open in general

why: #V_p(F_q) depends only on p mod q (congruence data); integral existence is not a finite-field point count. Rational V_p has n-independent cohomology.
Over ℚ (even ℤ[1/n]) U_n ≅ U_1 and U_1 has no integral points (4 > 3), so no rational-geometric input (ranks of fibrations) can force integral points; Siegel finiteness on genus-1 fibres. Sound.
A finite family set hitting every failure pattern = fixed finite slice menu, fails i.o. under H (B2 Thm 2.2(iii)).
Tiling encoding is a restatement of ES.

Ratio set {ab⁻¹ : ab|N} has ≤ τ(N)² ≈ polylog elements; BGK/sum-product needs power-size sets, so only e ≤ polylog is reachable, where it is the B4 covering problem (LONGSHOT Prop 1.4). The architecture is dead though 'known-false' is slightly loose.
Universal dichotomy statement refuted by explicit counterexamples (179/183 rich failures are poverty-type, not periodic; finite-range EVIDENCE but these are actual counterexamples).
Bounded-level quasi-modular main term + small error cannot vanish at all odd squares while M is ≫ there ((J)7 Thm 9.1, Serre–Stark); exact level series are theta quotients of growing level (Thm K).
SL₂ form of (★) verbatim (FRONTIER §2.1).
Finite core of identity families covering all large primes excluded by Mordell–Schinzel (square classes).
Markoff-type S_{p,D} integral point existence is MARKOFF_ES's restatement of ES; Fricke derivation is a dictionary lemma; Markoff precedent shows no general local-global principle.
Legendre phase in Jeffrey's formula is true calibration; non-vanishing over ES₅ words is ES₅.
Only fixed finite level menus are expressible in (ℕ,+,|) (4Cp is a product of variables); those sentences are false CONDITIONAL on H (B2(iii)).

Machiavelo–Tsopanidis uses power-size quaternion counts (M1a) and is true at squares; ES quaternion data are genus-layer (T1). Dead; 'known-false' for the specific reduction is loosely justified but plausibility 0 is right.
Sun's three-powers conjecture is a prime-value (parity) problem; the item's ES value is calibration only and the polarity inversion argument is right.
Fixed-p sieve over a polylog range of C is beyond all sieve technology; and P₂ shape doesn't give the class.
